description: Feature backlog - Product Owner owns priority

items.title: Archive-driven complexity estimation before item pick
items.intent: Before starting a sprint item, the orchestrator must consult historical archive data to estimate complexity and warn when an item resembles historically difficult work.
items.description: sprints.jsonl captures attempts, lines changed, and duration per completed item. Use this data to estimate complexity for queued items by matching on category and AC/step count. If historical items in the same category averaged more than 2 attempts, log an advisory note. Purely advisory — does not block or change behavior.
steps: Add estimate_complexity function that reads backlog/archive/sprints.jsonl
Group historical items by category; compute average attempts, duration, and lines changed per category
Before pick_item returns, call estimate_complexity with the picked item category and AC count
If estimated attempts exceed 2 or estimated duration exceeds 30 minutes, log_info an advisory complexity hint
Add a complexity column to print_batch_summary showing estimated vs actual attempts
Run shellcheck — zero new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: Before a sprint item starts, an advisory complexity hint is logged when historical data suggests the category is difficult
Items in categories with no historical data show no hint
The batch summary includes estimated vs actual attempts for each item
Complexity estimation does not block or delay sprint execution
shellcheck passes with zero new warnings
items.groomingNotes: Priority 'could' is correct — purely advisory, zero blocking behavior. User value: reduces surprise on hard items by surfacing historical difficulty before the sprint starts. The hint must never appear as an error or warning that implies the sprint should be skipped — it is informational only. AC are appropriately scoped. No dependencies. PO note: dependent on the modularization chain completing so that the script is in a stable state before adding new features; consider moving dependsOn to FEAT-059 to enforce this ordering. Batch summary column is secondary to the pre-sprint hint — if implementation time is limited, the hint alone satisfies user value.

items.title: Unify run and auto into single run command
items.intent: Eliminate the duplicate command surface — run becomes the only execution command, auto's scope behavior (done/p0/p1/p2) moves to run as optional arguments, auto-grooming activates when a scope is given
steps: Make cmd_run accept optional scope arg (done/p0/p1/p2) — when present, enables auto-grooming and circuit breaker
run with no scope defaults to one item (current run behavior)
run FEAT-001 targets specific item (current run ID behavior)
run done drains backlog (current auto done behavior)
Remove cmd_auto — fold its 28 lines of scope validation into cmd_run
Remove auto from main() dispatch, add scope args to run dispatch
Keep auto as hidden alias for backwards compat (just calls cmd_run)
Update help.txt
acceptanceCriteria: aishore run done works (drain backlog, auto-grooms)
aishore run p1 --limit 5 works (scoped with limit)
aishore auto done still works (hidden alias)

items.title: Streamline backlog edit flags
items.intent: Reduce backlog edit from 20+ flags to ~10 by collapsing the step/AC/scope array manipulation into simpler patterns — keep flags for scripting safety but remove the redundant clear/remove variants
steps: Replace --step/--clear-steps/--remove-step with --steps (JSON array or comma-separated, replaces entire array)
Replace --ac/--ac-verify/--clear-ac/--remove-ac with --ac (repeatable, replaces entire AC array when used)
Replace --scope/--clear-scope with --scope (replaces entire array when used)
Replace --depends-on/--clear-depends-on with --depends-on (replaces entire array when used)
Keep --title --intent --desc --priority --status --category --ready --no-ready --groomed-notes --groomed-at as-is
Update cmd_backlog_add to use same simplified patterns
Update help.txt
acceptanceCriteria: backlog edit FEAT-001 --ac 'criterion 1' --ac 'criterion 2' replaces all AC
backlog edit FEAT-001 --steps 'step 1' --steps 'step 2' replaces all steps
Existing backlog JSON is never corrupted — validation before write

items.title: Tiered help — compact default, deep per-command
items.intent: New users see a 10-15 line overview by default instead of 100+ lines — help <command> gives the deep dive, help --full gives the current exhaustive output
steps: Rewrite default help output to ~15 lines: core commands only (run, backlog, groom, status, init, help)
Add per-command help: aishore help run, aishore help backlog, etc — shows flags and examples for that command
Move current full help to aishore help --full
Update cmd_help to dispatch based on argument
acceptanceCriteria: aishore help fits in one terminal screen (< 20 lines)
aishore help run shows all run flags with descriptions
